transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-20 15:30 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Nimbus Head of ML), Ava Thompson (CTO), Rakesh Iyer (Platform Eng), Mei Chen (Compliance)

Summary:
Nimbus is evaluating model options for a risk-reporting assistant: heavy PDF ingestion, 40-60k effective context per session, multilingual support (EN, ES, FR), and tool-calling for live market quotes and internal ledger lookups. They are compliance-sensitive (financials), interested in Private/VPC but open to Dedicated if it meets data isolation and KMS/HSM requirements.

Topics:
- Context window needs and tradeoffs (64k target)
- Model selection: open models vs commercial LLMs (accuracy, hallucination)
- Tool-calling / function-calling for market data and signatures
- Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
- POC scope and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00:05] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, i'll kick off quick — main goal today is to map your constraints and suggest model+deployment options. Maya from our SE team will go deeper on perf.
[00:00:18] Carlos: hi thanks, i'm carlos. quick context — we ingest earnings reports and transaction feeds, typical session needs like 45k to 60k tokens of context when you expand to appendices, tables, etc — so context window is like top concern.
[00:00:34] Maya: got it, when you say 45k-60k is that after chunking and vector retrieval or contiguous context?
[00:00:40] Carlos: mostly contiguous, we want long-form QA with the whole doc sometimes plus conversation history; we also do tool calls to get live prices and to cross-check ledger entries.
[00:00:49] Ava: and from compliance side, we need either private deployment or dedicated instances with customer-managed KMS; no plaintext logs leaving our VPC.
[00:00:57] Mei: SOC2 and audit logs are musts — also retention policies and ability to redact PII on ingest.
[00:01:04] Priya: helpful, thanks. Jordan, quick thought — we often recommend a hybrid: dedicated for initial POC with strict networking, then decision toward private if audit requires full control.
[00:01:16] Jordan: yes that's typical. ok let's talk models — high level we think about three paths: 1) a high-context open model quantized for cost, 2) a commercial large-context model (e.g., vendor X style), or 3) a split pipeline: retrieval + smaller LM for reasoning.
[00:01:35] [00:01:38] Rakesh: can you expand on split pipeline? sounds like more infra.
[00:01:40] Maya: sure — you index documents, retrieve relevant chunks into a condensed prompt, and use a model with strong instruction-following. For very long context we can also use KV cache and prefix caching to avoid re-tokenizing the same legal boilerplate, so session cost drops.
[00:01:57] Rakesh: KV cache? do you mean K V cache or K V cash — just kidding — how persistent is that across requests?
[00:02:03] Maya: haha yeah the transcript might read weird — it's key-value cache, we can persist for session lifetime or longer with TTL and invalidate on doc updates.
[00:02:10] Carlos: we want near-real-time: user opens doc, asks question, backend does retrieval and maybe calls market-tool, latency under 800ms ideally for the first token. Is that realistic?
[00:02:21] Maya: for a 64k context on a heavy model, first-token in 800ms is challenging on Hosted; Dedicated with tuned batching and right GPUs gets closer. Also model choice matters: some open models optimized for long context are faster per token but may trade accuracy on finance domain.
[00:02:38] Jordan: to add, Redwood Optimize recommendations can pick quantization and batching that balance latency and cost — we'll share a rough calc.
[00:02:45] Ava: quick Q on tool-calling — we need to call our pricing engine and sign-on-ledger API, do you support signed function-calling or we need a gateway?
[00:02:53] Priya: Redwood supports structured function-calling patterns — you can define typed functions and we stream back structured responses. For secure APIs you can do function-calls from an SE-hosted connector or have your platform call the function using a short-lived token.
[00:03:07] Mei: are tokens stored by Redwood? that touches data residency.
[00:03:10] Jordan: for Hosted we store minimal metadata and we have opt-in retention and KMS managed keys; for Dedicated the keys and logs can stay in customer VPC with no egress. For Private/on-prem you'd control all keys. We'll send a diagram.
[00:03:22] [00:03:25] Carlos: model candidates — which open models should we evaluate for long context and low hallucination?
[00:03:29] Maya: Candidates we often try: Mistral-extended-window variants (good throughput), Llama-family long-context forks (quantizable), and a few newer high-context open weights. Also we can test co-opting a commercial long-context model as a reference. The key is run your evals on your prompt set.
[00:03:47] Rakesh: any gotchas with quantization and financial numeric fidelity? we need exact numbers sometimes.
[00:03:53] Maya: great point — int8 quantization can introduce small numeric oddities in reasoning; for finance we recommend mixed precision or per-layer calibration on sensitive tasks. Redwood's Optimize suggests per-workload quant profiles.
[00:04:05] Jordan: another tradeoff is model size vs latency — a 70B model might be more accurate on complex reasoning but slower; we can use a smaller reasoning model + retrieval for many cases.
[00:04:15] Ava: about multilingual — Spanish and French are secondaries. Do models degrade a lot?
[00:04:19] Maya: depends, many open models handle EN well; EN+ES+FR is usually okay but you should validate on your dataset — we can run evaluation across languages in the POC.
[00:04:29] Carlos: for the POC scope suggestion? what would Redwood propose?
[00:04:32] Jordan: propose a 6-week POC: week 1 intake and sample ingestion, weeks 2-3 baseline evals of 2-3 models with your prompts (hosted or dedicated infra), week 4 tool-calling integration, week 5 perf tuning and quantization testing, week 6 final report + cost/throughput recommendations.
[00:04:49] Rakesh: ok, what about SLA and uptime for Dedicated vs Private?
[00:04:53] Priya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and single-tenant GPU pools; private on-prem we give deployment scripts and support but SLA depends on customer ops — we do offer enterprise support packages.
[00:05:03] Mei: encryption and KMS — can Redwood integrate with our HSM?
[00:05:07] Maya: yes, for Dedicated we can bring-your-own-KMS and integrate with common HSMs; Private obviously you manage keys. We'll include a KMS integration checklist.
[00:05:16] [00:05:18] Carlos: sample throughput targets — we expect 50 concurrent users hitting long sessions during earnings windows; rough q: how to size GPU pools?
[00:05:26] Maya: we'll need to know average tokens/sec per session and synchronous vs async. For sync low-latency workflows you'll need more capacity; for off-peak batching we can autoscale. We'll estimate after you share samples.
[00:05:39] Jordan: on pricing, Hosted is per-token, Dedicated is commit + metered overage, Private is license + support. We'll provide a POC pricing worksheet.
[00:05:48] Carlos: any red flags we should be aware of regarding hallucination on financial statements?
[00:05:52] Maya: hallucinations are model and prompt-driven; for tables it's safer to use structured extraction and then reasoning step; tool-calling to verify numbers (e.g., call ledger) reduces risk. We also do regression tests in Redwood Optimize to catch quality regressions across deployments.
[00:06:10] Ava: ok good. can we see a quick demo of tool-calling and long-context performance?
[00:06:14] Jordan: we can schedule a demo — proposition: Maya runs a focused SE demo showing a 64k doc ingest + tool-call flow and latency numbers. Proposed slot next week.
[00:06:24] Rakesh: great. also want to involve our infra team to validate VPC peering and firewall rules.
[00:06:28] Priya: we'll include a network diagram and list of ports.
[00:06:31] Mei: last from compliance — need data residency matrix and proof of encryption in transit + at rest.
[00:06:36] Jordan: noted, we'll send the security pack and SOC2 report.
[00:06:40] [00:06:45] Wrap and recap
[00:06:46] Jordan: recap: deliver security pack + KMS checklist (Jordan), latency/cost estimates for 3 model candidates + deployment modes (Maya), Nimbus to send sample docs + throughput targets (Rakesh). Schedule demo and infra deep-dive.
[00:06:59] Carlos: thanks all, excited to see the numbers.
[00:07:02] Jordan: thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript
